visual: Three icons: name card, gift, bill; quick cuts
vo: Three everyday moments that feel different in China — none of them is about being polite.

visual: US doorway; young man calls older woman 'Linda'
vo: Names first. Your friend's mom has a first name. In the US, using it sounds friendly.

visual: CN doorway; same young man says '阿姨'; older woman relaxes
vo: In many Chinese families, the name you choose maps the relationship. 'Auntie' places you; her first name skips a step.

visual: Relationship map: family / neighbor / colleague's mom all become '阿姨'
vo: It's not about being formal. It's about where you stand.

visual: US birthday party; gift paper torn, confetti
vo: The same logic shows up at the door. In the US, tearing the paper off a gift is fun.

visual: CN home; gift received with both hands, thank-you first, set aside
vo: In many Chinese homes, the thank-you comes first; the gift can wait.

visual: Close-up: gift on table; two people talking
vo: It's not 'I don't care about the gift.' It's 'I care about you more than the thing.'
At the table, it changes again. In the US, a tip is part of the service.

visual: CN noodle shop; QR payment exact; owner waves off extra
vo: In China, the menu price is usually the whole price. Extra can feel less like generosity — more like charity.
Different rules. Same instinct: make the other person feel respected.

visual: Relationship map connects all three scenes
vo: The difference is what respect looks like.
